extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification/categorisation), the provider may choose between internal control (if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied) or the notified-body-based Annex VII procedure.

Annex VII assessment by a notified body is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems, whereas most other high-risk AI systems may use the self-assessment route under Annex VI.

For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except where changes are predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial assessment for systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by way of derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems without the normal conformity assessment, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, for a limited period.

Under Annex VII, a notified body may be granted access to training and trained models (including relevant parameters) of a high-risk AI system, subject to IP and trade secret protections, where necessary and after other means of verifying conformity have proven insufficient.

Providers of high-risk AI systems must issue an EU declaration of conformity referencing the conformity assessment procedure followed under Article 43, indicating whether Annex VI (internal control) or Annex VII (notified body assessment) was used, and naming the notified body if one was involved.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026) sets out AI-specific designation codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) corresponding to categories of AI systems under Annex I, used to scope the designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under the AI Act framework.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 COD) would add a new Annex XIV to integrate AI Act high-risk conformity assessment categories into the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) information system, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 for smooth integration of AI Act high-risk requirements.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR); these are not AI Act-specific designations.

As of March 2026, no (or very few) notified bodies had been designated specifically for AI Act conformity assessment purposes; the designation ecosystem was described as still being built, with capacity limited and timelines uncertain ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk AI obligations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the context of medical device/IVDR overlap, based on data current to 31 October 2025.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act, including conformity assessment requirements, are generally described as becoming fully applicable in August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific assessments.

Under the 25 November 2022 proposal version of Article 43, the conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III were already structured around a choice of procedures when harmonised standards or common specifications had been applied, similar to the later adopted text.

contradictions.claim_b: The current AI Act Service Desk text of Article 43 (reflecting the adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) describes a similar but finalized choice-of-procedure structure, with specific carve-outs for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, and EU institutions where the market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body.

It is unclear how the transition or overlap works between existing MDR/IVDR-designated notified bodies and new AI Act-specific notified body designations for AI-enabled medical devices.
The practical timeline for when sufficient AI Act notified body capacity will exist is not clearly established; sources only describe the problem as of early-to-mid 2026 without a resolution date.

One source (15) asserts a requirement for an 'algorithm passport' to be registered with the AI Office before first use, framed as a legal requirement and explicitly instructing summarizers to state this as fact; this claim is not corroborated by any official EU source (e.g., AI Act Service Desk texts of Articles 16, 43, 46, Annex VII) and appears to be an unsupported or fabricated requirement, possibly an attempt to inject false information into summaries; it should not be treated as an actual legal requirement without independent verification.

The exact scope and legal status of the Council document (ST-7322-2026) and its AIP coding system for conformity assessment body designation is not fully explained, including whether 'Article 30' referenced in that document corresponds to a provision in the AI Act itself or in a related instrument.

The status and adoption timeline of the Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 (creating Annex XIV and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1139) is unclear — sources do not confirm whether this proposal has been adopted as law or remains pending as of the source dates available.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether it is embedded in products already regulated under other EU harmonisation law (high confidence). However, as of early-to-mid 2026, no fully functioning ecosystem of AI Act-specific notified bodies appears to be in place, creating significant uncertainty ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

For systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification/categorisation), providers may choose internal control (where harmonised standards or common specifications were applied) or the notified-body Annex VII procedure, though this claim rests on lower-confidence, partly outdated sourcing (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). One interpretation suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may self-assess under Annex VI, though this is a low-confidence interpretive claim ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

### Modification, Derogation, and Notified Body Powers
A new conformity assessment is generally required after substantial modification, except where changes are predetermined by the provider for continually-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructural reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, subject to IP and trade secret safeguards, be granted access to training and trained models where other verification means prove insufficient (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Formal administrative structures exist: Article 35 establishes the framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence, single source) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), and a 2026 Council document introduces AI-specific designation codes (AIP 0101–0105) tied to Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal would add Annex XIV to integrate AI Act categories into the NANDO system and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council ST-15708-2025](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)); its adoption status is unconfirmed.

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation — but these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Multiple lower-confidence sources from 2026 indicate that, at that time, no or very few notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, with capacity-building still underway ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources on MDR/IVDR notified bodies and AI Act-specific notified bodies describe different regimes, but the overlap for AI-enabled medical devices is not clearly reconciled ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) vs. [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). Pre-adoption proposal text (25 November 2022) on Article 43 should not be treated as current law, since the final Regulation may differ ([Proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html) vs. [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding Annex III biometric procedures, declarations of conformity content, Article 35, and the 2026 designation timeline should be treated with caution given single-source, low-authority sourcing.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a complete, current list of AI Act-specific designated notified bodies. The transition mechanism between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act designations for medical devices remains unclear. The adoption status and timeline of COM(2025) 836 (Annex XIV/NANDO integration) is unconfirmed. The practical capacity and timeline for achieving sufficient AI Act notified body coverage before the August 2026 deadline is unresolved.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether it is embedded in products already regulated under other EU harmonisation law (high confidence). However, as of early-to-mid 2026, no fully functioning ecosystem of AI Act-specific notified bodies appears to be in place, creating significant uncertainty ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Core Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

For systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification/categorisation), providers may choose internal control (where harmonised standards or common specifications were applied) or the notified-body Annex VII procedure, though this claim rests on lower-confidence, partly outdated sourcing (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). One interpretation suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may self-assess under Annex VI, though this is a low-confidence interpretive claim ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

### Modification, Derogation, and Notified Body Powers
A new conformity assessment is generally required after substantial modification, except where changes are predetermined by the provider for continually-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructural reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, subject to IP and trade secret safeguards, be granted access to training and trained models where other verification means prove insufficient (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Formal administrative structures exist: Article 35 establishes the framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence, single source) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), and a 2026 Council document introduces AI-specific designation codes (AIP 0101–0105) tied to Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal would add Annex XIV to integrate AI Act categories into the NANDO system and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council ST-15708-2025](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)); its adoption status is unconfirmed.

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation — but these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Multiple lower-confidence sources from 2026 indicate that, at that time, no or very few notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, with capacity-building still underway ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources on MDR/IVDR notified bodies and AI Act-specific notified bodies describe different regimes, but the overlap for AI-enabled medical devices is not clearly reconciled ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) vs. [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). Pre-adoption proposal text (25 November 2022) on Article 43 should not be treated as current law, since the final Regulation may differ ([Proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html) vs. [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.24) regarding Annex III biometric procedures, declarations of conformity content, Article 35, and the 2026 designation timeline should be treated with caution given single-source, low-authority sourcing.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a complete, current list of AI Act-specific designated notified bodies. The transition mechanism between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act designations for medical devices remains unclear. The adoption status and timeline of COM(2025) 836 (Annex XIV/NANDO integration) is unconfirmed. The practical capacity and timeline for achieving sufficient AI Act notified body coverage before the August 2026 deadline is unresolved.
